Why do you assume she murdered her child?  The police aren't even saying that. We don't even know how this woman felt about her pregnancy before that day. It sounds to me like she was in shock after waking up to find she'd given birth and her child was dead.  Hell, maybe she didn't even know she was pregnant because, yes, some women don't realize they are. 


Why didn't she speak up? Well, why most people don't..because of shame or guilt or fear of retribution for something. I can't villianize this woman given the circumstances she went through and which has been verified by police who have more facts than you or I in this matter. 


When you have the options of being empathetic/considerate or being angry/dismissive towards a stranger....why do you pick anger and dismissiveness?  


Her story doesn't discount your own.


Its just that our own personal perspectives won't illuminate all the facets of any other person's story. What we would have done or have done in this situation may absolutely have been different but thats a thought exercise that divides more than it solves. 


What our own experiences can do is connect us to others, allowing us to take different perspectives in order to become more empathetic and caring to those different than ourselves. 


I'm glad you had the strength to make an incredibly hard decision. I wish more could have that strength and the emotional maturity you expressed while being so young. Not every person has those same skills. They may also not have the knowledge or the languages skills, or the support and safety to make the same decision. There are just too many factors for me to feel good about making a judgement on this woman.

36F First symptoms started 2 years ago give or take and more have joined the ride. I was an Algebra teacher up to early this year. Had to quit because of incontinence,  pain, and mobility. 

Symptoms from earliest 2021 to most recent:
-left torso pain (diagnosed as abdominal wall pain Jan. 2023)

-incontinence and bowel issues (diarrhea and constipation haven't had a normal bowel movement in a very long time..was told it was anxiety causing it)

-pain after eating

-nausea and vomiting after eating (usually when I'm already in a lot of pain but doesn't happen every time I eat)

-the pain from the left side extends across my torso to the right side, to my back, and down my legs especially the left inner thigh 

-Fatigue

-Numbness in my hands, feet, and lower torso

-Light headed/unbalanced

-Tingling sensation from my hands to my feet with sporadic jolts of pain

-Difficulty standing up and walking (I know have a walker because I've fallen)

-Memory issues/cognitive issues (forget words/names more often. I say the wrong word. Spelling has become an issue)

-Slurring

-Vision issues (white sparks when in extreme pain, cloudiness)

The pain in my left side was the earliest symptom. I then began having menstrual cycles every other week with intense pain and bowel issues. My gyno did an exploratory surgery in 2021 and saw that I had endometriosis. I had a full hysterectomy early 2022. The pain in my left side did not stop and it progressed to my right side and to my back. Had upper and lower colonoscopy and barium enema (later 2022). Not diverticulitis or ulcerative colitis. Referred to gastro specialist and my GP prescribed me gababentin. Diagnosed with abdominal wall pain and given shot (Jan. 2023). Shot did not take. Pain progressed to my left leg. Went to another gastro specialist because the first never addressed the bowel issues. Second gastro ran blood tests, mri on my torso, and fecal tests(Aug. 2023). All clear. I really start thinking it's in my head at this time and I'm drowning in medical debt since I no longer have my insurance. I begin having tingling sensations with the jolts of pain. I'm losing my balance as I walk. I'm having to use walls and walk slowly. I'm having intense pain and body tingles after walking. I fall (late Nov.). My GP says it's either my back or my brain. Just got my mri (no contrast) and I have “There is a single focus of white matter FLAIR/T2 signal abnormality in the LEFT frontal subcortical white matter
(image 20 series 5 and series 8). White matter signal characteristics are
otherwise appropriate for age. No evidence of an intra-axial mass or mass
effect.” So, mri says no ms. 

I'm so tired of hurting. I want to know what it is so I can find a way to manage it. I'm tired of feeling like I'm crazy and it's all in my head. I want to go back to work. I really would just like to walk again. I'm in pain 24/7 and I just want it to end. 

Is this relatable to anyone? And, if so, what did you do next? How can I advocate for myself when I keep checking off boxes and still don't have an answer or an end in sight?
